description_en: Interlaced basket weave gives this black sweater a woven, almost architectural surface. Knitted in a cotton blend and shaped to a regular fit, it sits easily over a crisp white oxford shirt with the collar left out.

Broad bands of colour run across the body, framed by an open collar that leaves the neck bare. Cotton in a regular fit, offered in green and white or white and navy. Over a plain white tee with pleated chinos, it keeps winter dressing relaxed.

Thin nautical stripes cross a white ground in blue or brown on this cotton long sleeve. A regular fit keeps the line straight from shoulder to hem. Under an unbuttoned overshirt with stone trousers, the stripe shows just enough.

Interrupted black-and-white stripes break across a chunky knit, giving the pattern a hand-drawn rhythm. Slim through the body, the cotton blend keeps the heavy texture from adding bulk. Wear it with black tailored trousers and white leather sneakers.

Blocks of colour meet across a brushed cotton knit with a soft, slightly hazy surface. The oversized cut gives it room through the body and arms. In navy or red, it sits well over straight-leg jeans and suede chukka boots.

Stripes softened by a brushed surface run across this wool blend crew neck. Cut oversized, it carries an easy, roomy shape for winter weekends. Available in beige or green, it works over a checked flannel shirt left open at the neck.

Buttons at a henley placket open the neckline of this cotton knit. The oversized shape keeps it loose and unstructured, in blue or green. Throw it on over a white thermal top with relaxed cargo trousers for a weekend at home or out.

Raised cables run the length of this wool crew neck, giving the front depth and shadow. A regular fit leaves room for a collared shirt beneath. In navy, it pairs with grey flannel trousers and brown brogues for the office.

Twisted cable columns define this cotton blend crewneck, cut slim for a close, tidy line. It comes in five shades, from off-white through to burgundy. Burgundy reads sharp under a camel overcoat with charcoal trousers.

Polo collar above, cable-knit body below: this wool sweater sits between smart and casual. Regular fit, in black, blue or white. Under a suede bomber with dark chinos, the white version suits a dinner out.

Above a cable-knit front, a quarter-zip neck finishes this beige sweater. Regular fit, cotton blend; zip it to the chin or leave it open at the throat. Layer it beneath a quilted gilet with dark selvedge jeans.

Cable panels alternate with stripes across this slim wool polo sweater, giving the front a structured pattern. The polo collar frames the face neatly. Green works well with cream wide-leg trousers and loafers.

Set into olive knit, a camouflage panel gives this sweater a utilitarian edge. A slim cut in cotton blend keeps the military reference sharp rather than bulky. Combine it with black cargo trousers and lace-up boots.

Deep, chunky ribs give this light grey crew neck strong texture and a defined shape. The regular fit, in a cotton blend, keeps it straightforward. It holds its own over a white button-down with charcoal wool trousers and dark derbies.

Waffle-knit squares give this black wool crewneck a gridded, three-dimensional surface. The chunky gauge and regular fit make it a winter top layer in its own right. Under a long grey overcoat, it needs nothing more than black jeans.

Fine-gauge knit and a slim fit keep this light grey crewneck close and smooth. Cotton blend, plain round neck, no ornament. It slides under a navy blazer as neatly as it sits alone with tailored trousers.

Folded high at the neck and cut slim, this turtleneck brings a strong vertical line to winter tailoring. The cotton blend knit comes in eleven colourways. Camel worn under a dark double-breasted coat is a strong place to start.

Black and white meet in clean-edged blocks across a ribbed knit, giving this slim sweater a graphic presence. The cotton blend keeps the rib defined. Grey wool trousers and black Chelsea boots let the contrast lead.

Red Breton stripes on white give this slim knit a bright, maritime contrast. The cotton blend holds a neat shape from neck to cuff. Over pale blue jeans with canvas sneakers, it carries into a sunny winter afternoon.

Contrast detailing marks the V-neck of this wool sweater, drawing the eye to the neckline. Regular fit, in black or light blue. Put it over a striped poplin shirt and under a tweed jacket for a layered office look.

A corduroy collar sits on top of a quarter-zip placket, mixing woven ridges with soft knit. The cotton blend body is cut oversized, in beige or white. Pair it with brown corduroy trousers for a tonal study in texture.

Knitted wales echo the look of corduroy across this cotton crewneck, giving it a ridged, tactile front. Regular fit, available in brown among other shades. The brown version teams with a waxed jacket and dark denim on cold weekends.

Diagonal lines run across the surface of this crew neck, catching light at an angle. The polyester knit is cut oversized for an easy, roomy shape. In off-white, it lifts a dark wool overcoat and black trousers.

Worked into white cotton blend knit, a diamond pattern reads clearly up close and subtle from across a room. The oversized cut adds ease through the body. Contrast it with charcoal pleated trousers and black loafers.

Distressed ribbing gives this camel crewneck a lived-in character from the first wear. A regular fit in cotton blend, with a texture that looks deliberately worn. Put it with washed black jeans and rugged lace-up boots.

Deliberately rough, the distressed texture of this black cotton knit reads raw rather than refined. An oversized cut adds to the loose, unpolished shape. Layer it over a longline white tee and black cargos.
Washing softens the dark grey of this wool knit, while distressing adds a broken, vintage surface. Oversized for an easy winter shape. It sits well with ecru denim and a worn leather jacket.

A fine dobby texture gives the surface of this long sleeve top a subtle, repeating pattern. Cotton blend in a regular fit, in camel or white. Tuck the white version into pleated trousers beneath an unstructured blazer.

Slender cables run in tight columns across this white sweater, keeping the texture refined rather than heavy. The cotton blend is cut slim to follow the body. Set it against navy chinos and brown suede loafers.

Mint is the unexpected choice in this fine-knit polyester crewneck, offered alongside a quieter beige. Cut slim, it lies flat under a light overshirt or sits neatly over white trousers with tan loafers.

Beige fine knit, a round neck and long sleeves make this a base layer that works under nearly anything. Regular fit, in cotton blend. Try it under a brown leather jacket with olive chinos for an earthy, tonal combination.
Close vertical ribs line this cotton crewneck from neck to hem, giving it a gently lined surface. Regular fit, in beige or navy. In navy, it sits under a camel car coat with tan suede boots.

Dark grey and generously oversized, this fine rib crewneck takes a looser view of a familiar shape. The polyester knit carries narrow ribbing throughout. Wear it with black wide-leg trousers and chunky trainers.

Ribbing in a fine gauge gives this long sleeve crewneck a close, textured surface without bulk. Cotton blend, regular fit, in beige or black. The black works under a charcoal suit in place of a shirt.

Soft and fuzzy at the surface, this brown crewneck has a tactile, almost brushed look. Cut slim in a cotton blend, it keeps that texture close to the body. Pair it with off-white wool trousers and brown suede derbies.
Hazy texture and a polo collar define this brown cotton sweater. The oversized cut gives it a relaxed, easy shape with room to move. Set it over a white tee with loose-fit jeans and penny loafers.

In blue with a fuzzy, softly blurred knit, this polo sweater frames the neck with a neat collar. Regular fit, cotton blend. It works tucked loosely into grey trousers with a brown belt and suede shoes.
Jacquard-knitted geometry patterns this camel sweater from shoulder to hem. Cotton blend, cut slim so the motif lies flat and reads clearly. It sits neatly under a dark peacoat with black jeans.

Graphic cables, arranged as a bold motif, run across this polo sweater beneath a collared neck. The cotton blend is cut oversized, in olive or light blue among other shades. Olive with chocolate pleated trousers makes a rich, earthy pairing.

Two-tone graphic stripes, in black and white or beige and white, run across this cotton blend knit. A regular fit keeps the proportions straightforward. The black version suits grey jeans and a dark suede jacket.

A half-zip rises into a short mock neck on this slim wool knit, giving the collar line structure. Six colourways, including brown and mint. Worn open over a denim shirt, the brown carries well into evening.
Ribs turned horizontal stack across this dark grey cotton crewneck, creating a banded, linear surface. Regular fit throughout. It anchors a tonal outfit built on charcoal trousers and black boots.
Dropped shoulders and horizontal ribbing give this sweater a relaxed, softened line within a regular fit. Cotton blend, in beige or black. Beige suits light-wash denim and brown desert boots.

Off-white and black stripes run across this cotton blend crewneck, finished with pocket detail. The regular fit keeps it easy and familiar. It goes with black chinos and white canvas plimsolls for days in town.

Jacquard stripes are knitted into the body of this black crewneck, so the pattern sits within the fabric rather than on it. Polyester, cut oversized. Combine it with a long black coat and loose black trousers for a single-colour look.
Melange yarn flecks this crewneck with subtle variation, so even the blue reads layered rather than flat. Cotton blend, regular fit. Wear it with khaki chinos and white sneakers on off-duty days.

Micro ribs give this long sleeve a fine, close texture, while the oversized, relaxed cut lets it hang loose. Available in beige or black, in a cotton blend. Layer the black one under an open shacket with relaxed denim.

Pared back to a round neck and pocket detail, this beige crewneck relies on proportion alone. Cut oversized in polyester knit, it takes on a roomy shape. Team it with tapered olive trousers and white trainers.
Subtle surface texture is the only detail on this black crewneck. Oversized and cut in polyester, it keeps its outline simple and loose. It sits under a black bomber jacket with grey tapered joggers.

Nine shades, from camel and olive to red and navy, in a ribbed cotton knit shaped to sit close to the head without pressing. One size. The camel version looks right with a charcoal overcoat and a grey wool scarf on winter mornings.

Box logo detail on a close ribbed cotton beanie. One size, in brown or white. The white one makes a sharp point of contrast against a black puffer jacket and dark jeans, while the brown stays softer and more tonal.

Cotton rib knit with an embroidered logo detail, one size. Six colours cover white, light grey, dark grey and black, alongside beige and olive. Olive pairs naturally with a cream fisherman sweater and worn-in mid-blue denim.

Here the rib knit carries a patch logo detail. Cotton, one size, and available in red, navy, olive, brown and white. Red adds a single strong colour to an otherwise all-grey tracksuit worn with white trainers.

Faux leather in a utility shape, drawn in at the waist by a belt. The oversized cut leaves space for thicker layers underneath. In black or brown, it works over a grey marl hoodie with straight black trousers for colder days.

Biker styling in faux leather, cut slim through the body and sleeves so it follows the shoulder line closely. Black keeps it familiar; white makes it sharper and less expected. Put it over a plain white tee, black slim jeans and Chelsea boots.

Built in faux leather, this aviator has a shearling-style collar that closes with a buckle. Regular fit, in beige or black. Turned up against the wind, the collar frames a chunky roll neck, worn here with dark straight-leg jeans.

The bomber in its most direct form: black leather, regular fit, no added detail. Its strength is proportion and material rather than ornament. For winter evenings, it sits well over a grey crewneck sweater and charcoal wool trousers.

Denim trucker jacket with a regular fit and the recognisable workwear shape. Offered in brown or light grey, it reads softer than standard denim. Layer it over a plaid flannel shirt with cream chinos.

Black leather with no surface detail breaking up the silhouette. An oversized fit lets the jacket hang loose and drape from the shoulders. Wear it open over a black knit polo and pleated grey trousers.
Canvas in cotton, with a collar in a contrasting tone and a regular fit. Available in camel, off-white and olive. The olive pairs easily with an ecru tee, tan chinos and brown suede desert boots.

Fireman clasps line the front of this oversized cotton jacket, set against a contrast collar. In beige, it carries a clear workwear character. Throw it on over a navy hoodie and loose light-wash jeans.

Navy cotton, cut oversized, with a collar in contrast colour and a row of fireman clasps. The deep tone keeps the hardware looking sharp rather than rugged. Try it with a striped Breton top and off-white trousers.
Harrington lines in cotton, with a corduroy collar in a contrasting shade. Regular fit, in off-white or olive. A fine-gauge merino crewneck and grey flannel trousers give it a smarter edge.

Coach jacket in olive polyester, set off by a contrasting faux leather collar. Regular fit, with an easy, straight shape. Combine it with a white heavyweight tee, black cargo trousers and chunky runners.

Beige corduroy brings texture to the Harrington shape, cut oversized for a relaxed line across the shoulders. A good choice for winter weekends. It sits comfortably with dark indigo jeans and penny loafers.

Corduroy in black, oversized, fastened with fireman clasps. The ridged cord surface softens the hardware and keeps the dark colour from looking flat. Match it with a charcoal sweatshirt and black wide-leg trousers.

Brown corduroy with a hood and fireman clasps down the front. The oversized body takes a thick knit beneath without strain. Good over an oatmeal sweater with khaki work trousers when the temperature drops.
Cut short at the waist, this black faux leather jacket shows more of the trouser line. Regular fit, sharp and compact. It suits high-rise pleated trousers with a white shirt tucked in.

White striped cotton, cropped short and cut oversized, closed with fireman clasps. The boxy proportion balances wider trousers well. Over a pale blue oxford shirt with wide ecru trousers, it looks deliberate and light.

Diagonal twill weave gives this dark grey zip jacket visible texture up close. Polyester, regular fit, with a neat and understated profile. It works over a black merino roll neck with tailored charcoal trousers.

Diamond quilting runs across a green bomber in cotton blend. Regular fit through the body, with a familiar, compact bomber outline. Over a cream cable-knit sweater with navy trousers, it reads country rather than city.

Distressed black leather gives this zip-up a lived-in surface from the first day. The oversized fit adds ease and weight to the silhouette. Wear it over a faded grey tee with black straight jeans and broken-in boots.

Embossing marks out the surface of this brown faux leather bomber. Its oversized fit keeps the shape loose and current. Worn over an ecru knitted crewneck with dark brown trousers, it builds a warm tonal outfit.

Burgundy faux leather, oversized, with embroidered detailing. A rich colour for winter that needs little support from the rest of the outfit. Keep everything else black: a black tee and black tapered trousers.

Fading softens this brown denim jacket, cut slim so it stays close to the body. The fading gives it a softer, worn character from new. Over a white henley with black jeans, the brown becomes the focus.

Olive faux leather in a straightforward bomber cut. Regular fit, with enough room for a sweatshirt underneath and a shape that stays neat. Team it with a heather-grey sweatshirt, khaki chinos and white low-top trainers.

Roomy and oversized, this black faux leather zip-up keeps things plain. Simple enough for daily wear, strong enough to anchor an outfit. It sits easily over a striped rugby top and light grey wide-leg trousers.
Grained brown leather shaped into a bomber, cut oversized. The grain catches light and gives depth to the colour. Worn with a denim shirt buttoned to the top and dark olive trousers.
Herringbone weave in light or dark grey, shaped as a utility zip jacket. Polyester, regular fit. Pull it over a navy quarter-zip knit and charcoal wool trousers for a quietly smart weekday look.

Ribbed at the hem, this black leather bomber holds neatly at the waist. Cut to a regular fit, it keeps a short, sharp outline. A burgundy crewneck and pale grey trousers bring colour against the black.

Leather-effect jacket in brown faux leather, with a detachable collar that changes its character in seconds. The fit is oversized. With the collar on, layer it over a shawl-collar cardigan and corduroy trousers.

Structured and closed with fireman clasps, this black faux leather jacket has a smooth leather-effect finish. Regular fit, more structured than casual. Over a mock-neck knit and slim grey trousers, the clasps become the only detail needed.

Overshirt in shape and olive leather in material, it is cut oversized so it can be worn open or closed. It sits between a shirt and a jacket in weight and spirit. Over a fine merino tee and relaxed beige trousers, it stays light.

Pared down to a clean placket and a straight body, this polyester button-up jacket lets its shape do the work. Regular fit, in black, light grey or navy. The navy one works with a crisp white shirt and navy tailored trousers for a tonal office outfit.
Nothing distracts from the line of this cotton blend zip-up, cut to a regular fit. Beige, black or navy. Match the beige with a white piqué polo and navy drawstring trousers.

Knitwear texture, jacket structure: ribbing runs through this polyester zip-up. Regular fit, in beige, brown or light grey. Brown looks good with a tonal beige knit and light-wash jeans for an easy weekend outfit.
Ruched sleeves gather along the arms of this black bomber, adding texture where most bombers stay plain. Cotton blend, slim fit. Wear it with slim black trousers and white leather low-tops.
Warmth at the neck comes from a shearling-style collar on this beige faux leather jacket, cut to a regular fit. A brown corduroy shirt and dark jeans keep the whole outfit in warm, natural tones.
An aviator in dark grey faux fur, with shearling-style trim edging the jacket. Slim fit, so it stays close and neat despite the texture. Pair it with black needlecord trousers and lace-up boots.
Suede-effect polyester reworks the chore jacket with a soft, matte surface. Regular fit, in black, dark grey or navy. Navy over a chambray shirt and grey trousers keeps it relaxed but tidy.

Brushed and matte, black suede-effect polyester makes a neat zip jacket with a regular fit. The brushed surface adds depth that plain black often lacks. It pairs simply with a white long-sleeve tee and charcoal joggers.
Moto styling meets a textured polyester surface in this regular-fit jacket. Offered in beige, black and light grey. The light grey reads crisp against a fitted black tee and grey denim.

Textured stripes run through this cotton blend zip-up, visible up close and subtle from a distance. Regular fit, in beige or navy. Zip the navy halfway over a grey marl tee, with beige corduroy trousers below.
Utility styling on a white puffer, in polyester and a regular fit. Bright and graphic, it stands out on grey winter days. Contrast it with a black ribbed knit, dark joggers and trail trainers.
Mint, off-white and olive: this cotton utility zip jacket comes in a regular fit. Light in look and practical in shape. The mint brings fresh colour to a grey crewneck and ecru jeans.

Vintage character defines this burgundy leather utility jacket, cut oversized. The deep colour gives it presence without any extra detail. Over a cream heavy knit with black jeans, it holds the outfit together.
Stand collar, camel faux leather and a vintage profile: the jacket keeps its detail to the neckline. The cut is oversized and easy. Combine it with a navy crew-neck knit and cream trousers.
Trucker shape meets faux leather here, with a vintage feel. The fit is oversized, in black or camel. Camel over a checked shirt and light-wash jeans gives it a relaxed, lived-in character.
Slim and close in shape, this brown denim jacket carries a vintage wash. The washed finish looks broken in from the start. Layer it over a cream waffle-knit top and black trousers.
Grey faux suede, washed for a softer, slightly uneven tone. The oversized fit lets it hang loosely and move with the body. Try it with an off-white knit polo and charcoal trousers.
Washed brown faux leather, finished to look aged and softened rather than new. Oversized fit with an easy drape. Worn with an olive sweatshirt and stone trousers for a muted palette.
Acid wash gives this blue cotton tee a mottled, uneven colour. Long sleeves and an oversized fit add ease. Worn under an open overshirt with black jeans, it adds texture to a simple outfit.

Long sleeves, a crewneck and a slim cut in cotton blend, shaped to sit smoothly under other layers. Available in beige, black, mint and white. Black goes neatly under a quilted gilet with dark chinos.

Vertical ribs run the length of this cotton long sleeve tee, lengthening the torso visually. Slim fit, in beige, black, brown or white. Brown sits well under an unbuttoned cardigan with grey trousers.

Embroidered detail sits on washed cotton, cut oversized with long sleeves. Beige, light blue or olive, each softened by the wash. Light blue looks easy with relaxed cream trousers and canvas sneakers.

Fine horizontal stripes run across a ribbed cotton blend henley, cut slim with a short placket at the neck. The off-white and brown colourway sits well under an open chore jacket with straight-leg chinos.

Waffle knit gives this long-sleeve henley a grid texture that catches the light. Cotton blend, slim through the body and arms, in five shades including navy and light grey. Under a field jacket, it carries a winter weekend.

Cotton jogger sweatpants in green, slim through the leg and gathered at the ankle. The classic shape, with nothing added and nothing missing. A plain crewneck sweatshirt and leather sneakers complete an easy winter morning.

Piping traces the side of each leg on these camel cotton joggers, a tailored line on a casual garment. The slim fit keeps the silhouette narrow. A fine-gauge knit and suede loafers move them toward the evening.

Campus references meet a slim jogger: cotton sweatpants with logo detail, offered in black, off-white and white. The leg narrows toward the ankle for a sharp profile. A plain hoodie and high-top sneakers finish the line.
These wide-leg sweatpants come in beige cotton, washed for a soft, lived-in tone. The baggy fit falls straight and generous from hip to hem. A cropped boxy tee and chunky trainers balance the volume.

Cut wide through the leg, these brown cotton sweatpants have a baggy fit that moves freely. The volume reads deliberate rather than loose. With a fitted dark knit and leather derbies, they hold their own beyond the weekend.

Deep ribs in a chunky wool blend give this button cardigan real weight and structure. The oversized cut sits loose through the body, in brown or off-white. Worn open over a roll neck and dark wool trousers, it anchors a winter outfit.

An open knit lets air and light through this wool blend cardigan, finished with a soft collar. Oversized and loose, it comes in black or yellow. The yellow reads strongest over a plain cotton tee and pleated trousers.

One zip runs the full length of this blue ribbed cardigan in cotton blend. Regular fit: close enough to layer under a coat, easy enough to wear open. Over an oxford shirt it bridges the office and the weekend.
Part polo, part cardigan: a ribbed cotton blend knit that pairs a polo collar with a cardigan front, in a clear yellow. Regular fit. Cord trousers and brogues give it a relaxed, collegiate edge.

Slim ribbed cotton blend knit, with a contrast collar that frames the face. Available in brown, navy and white. Under an unstructured blazer with flannel trousers, it replaces a shirt and tie without losing polish.

Contrast stitching outlines the chest pocket and seams of this slim knit polo in cotton blend. Black or white, each colour makes the stitching read differently. Tucked into pleated chinos with a leather belt, it looks finished.

Wool knit, long sleeves and a polo collar: a precise layer for winter. The regular fit leaves room beneath a long overcoat, and six colours run from white to dark grey. Tapered trousers keep the line clean underneath.

Sweatshirt comfort with a polo collar and a quarter-zip at the neck. Soft cotton in an oversized cut, offered in brown, navy and olive. Relaxed cargo trousers and trail runners suit its practical character.

Black ribbed cotton, a half-zip collar and long sleeves, cut slim to follow the body. It reads sharper than a sweatshirt and easier than a shirt. Slim dark jeans and chelsea boots keep the outfit tonal.

Close ribbing runs the length of this long-sleeve cotton polo, cut slim through the chest and arms. Four colours, from white to olive. Under a corduroy overshirt it adds texture on texture without bulk.
Flat and wide at the neck, an open collar defines this black ribbed polo. Cotton, slim fit, long sleeves. Beneath a double-breasted blazer it makes a strong case for dinner without a tie.

White wool with a raised, textured knit and a zip at the collar. The oversized cut gives the polo an easy drape across the shoulders and chest. Wide-leg trousers and leather mules match its relaxed proportion.

Vertical ribs lengthen the torso on this slim cotton polo in white, finished with an open collar. The rib also keeps the knit close without clinging. Worn with a dark suit and no tie, it sharpens the evening.

Terry cotton with vertical stripes, cut oversized for an easy, boxy shape. Light grey runs against black or mint, depending on the colourway. Loose drawstring trousers and slides make it a home-to-street layer.
Light grey waffle texture and an open collar define this slim cotton polo. The grid surface adds depth even in a single tone. Under a quilted gilet it holds up on a cold winter afternoon.

Oversized lettering is woven into this cotton jacquard scarf in light grey and black. The graphic stays crisp because it sits in the weave, not on the surface. Thrown over a dark wool overcoat, it does the talking. One size.

Brown and beige monograms run on the diagonal across this cotton scarf, giving the pattern movement. One size, easy to knot or drape. Tied loosely at the collar of a trench coat, it adds warmth and a point of interest.

Interlocking lines form a maze across this cotton scarf, rendered in black and brown. The geometry reads graphic up close and tonal from a distance. Looped once around the neck of a peacoat, the one-size scarf sits neatly.

Florals and monograms combine in a heritage pattern of dark grey and camel. The one-size cotton is soft enough to fold close at the throat. Draped under the lapels of a tweed jacket, it brings colour without noise.
Soft off-white cotton, finished at each end with a loose fringe. A single pale tone makes this scarf the lightest element in a winter outfit. Against a dark puffer jacket, the contrast does the work.

Woven in jacquard, a repeating monogram runs through this cotton scarf, light grey against black. The pattern has a quiet regularity that suits tailoring and sportswear alike. Tucked into a shearling-collar jacket, it closes the neckline.

Ornamental dots scatter across a brown and beige ground on this cotton scarf. The print feels old-world without turning fussy. Paired with a corduroy blazer, the warm tones line up naturally. One size, for winter.

Beige cotton in a single tone, ending in a light fringe at both edges. Cut in a single size and neutral enough to sit with almost any coat. Worn long and loose over a denim jacket, it gives a casual outfit some length.

Lettering patterns this cotton scarf in brown and camel, a warm pairing that suits the season. Light enough to wrap twice, full enough to show the design. With a chunky knit and a suede jacket, it stays in the same palette.
Yellow against black, with logo detail across the cotton. This scarf is meant to be seen, so the rest can stay plain. Against a dark parka, the yellow catches the eye from a distance.
Loose brushstrokes in blue cross a beige cotton ground, like a painted canvas turned sweatshirt. Regular fit, true to its proportions. Straight raw denim and canvas sneakers let the artwork lead.
Bandana paisley, the print of workwear and western shirts, set on white cotton. The oversized fit keeps it relaxed and roomy. Faded denim and work boots stay faithful to the pattern's roots.
Plain cotton, oversized cut, no graphics. This sweatshirt comes in black, light grey and white and covers the basics with ease. Under a hooded parka it adds warmth without adding bulk at the neck.

Collegiate graphics on light grey cotton, in an oversized cut with a sporting attitude. The varsity look carries weekend energy without trying too hard. Track pants and retro runners keep it true to its athletic origins.

The word Dreamer anchors the graphic on this oversized cotton sweatshirt, in green or light grey. Roomy through the body and sleeves. With relaxed carpenter trousers it settles into an easy off-duty uniform.

Panelled construction in off-white and pink, with a polo collar on an oversized cotton sweatshirt. The colour blocking does the design work. Light-wash wide jeans and suede trainers keep it soft and casual.

Solid olive cotton and a round crewneck, cut oversized with room through the body. The earthy shade works as a neutral across a winter wardrobe. Dark chinos and desert boots keep the palette grounded.
Panel seams trace the front of this off-white crewneck, adding structure to a simple shape. Cotton blend, regular fit. Under a single-breasted wool coat, the paneling keeps the outfit sharp.

Pinstripes run through a ribbed cotton blend, giving this sweatshirt a tailored undertone. Regular fit, in black or light grey. With tailored trousers and loafers it sits comfortably in a smart-casual office.

Softened at the shoulder by raglan sleeves, this beige cotton crewneck runs in one line from collar to cuff. The oversized fit adds ease across the chest and shoulders. Wide corduroy trousers continue its relaxed, vintage-sport mood.

Raw edges and a short mock neck give this oversized cotton sweatshirt an unfinished, deliberate look. Available in beige, black and light grey. Under a technical shell jacket it bridges street and outdoor.
Mint cotton with exposed raw edges, cut oversized for a loose, dropped feel. The soft colour plays against the rough detailing. Relaxed light denim and canvas high-tops suit its streetwear stance.
Set into the side seam, a zip is the detail that marks out this ribbed sweatshirt. Mint cotton blend, regular fit. With slim tailored joggers and minimal sneakers, the look stays clean and sporty.

Jacquard texture builds a raised pattern across this polyester crewneck, offered in beige, black, light grey and white. The fit is regular. Over a collared shirt, the points framing the neckline, it reads smart.

Trouble Maker set across black cotton, cut oversized. The message carries the attitude, while the plain ground keeps it controlled. Distressed denim and combat boots lean into the edge for winter nights.
Varsity cues meet a zip detail on this oversized polyester sweatshirt, in dark grey or white. Sporty, roomy and graphic. A baseball cap and straight jeans complete the off-campus feel.

Ribbed velvet gives this slim crewneck a rich surface that shifts with the light. Five colours, from camel to red. Flat-front trousers and suede chelsea boots make it an evening alternative to a shirt.

A V-inset at the neckline recalls old athletic sweatshirts, here in an oversized cotton blend. Beige or green, both with a worn-in vintage feel. Faded straight jeans and leather sneakers keep it honest.
Vintage washing gives this green cotton crewneck a faded, broken-in surface from the first wear. The fit is oversized and easy. Beneath a canvas work jacket it suits cold mornings outdoors.

Raglan sleeves and a vintage wash combine on an oversized cotton sweatshirt offered in mauve or olive. The faded tones look found rather than new. With dark cords and a beanie, the mood stays laid-back.
Darkness is the graphic on this washed cotton sweatshirt, a hard word set on soft mint or pink. The oversized fit adds slouch. Wide cargo trousers and skate shoes match its street register.
Mauve cotton, washed for a gentle fade, in a loose oversized crewneck. Colour leads here, so the shape stays simple. Relaxed jeans and suede trainers give it an unforced weekend ease.

Undulating waves are knitted into the surface of this oversized cotton blend crewneck, in beige or green. The texture gives depth from across the room. Under an open overshirt, the pattern still shows through.

Chukka height meets a chunky sole on these lace-up leather boots, built with weight and grip for winter streets. Offered in brown and camel, they run true to size. They sit naturally with cuffed dark denim and a chunky cable-knit sweater.

Beige suede and a deep, chunky sole give the Chelsea profile a heavier, more grounded stance. The light tone keeps it from feeling bulky. Try them with wide-leg wool trousers and a belted overcoat for a tonal look. Take your usual size.

Grained black leather brings texture and resilience to a streamlined Chelsea silhouette. The surface shrugs off winter wear while keeping a polished line under tailoring. Slip them on beneath slim wool trousers and a dark overcoat; sizing runs true.

Leather uppers on a raised, chunky sole make this a Chelsea boot with weight behind every step. Black reads sharp and brown more relaxed, and both fit true to size. Team them with straight-leg chinos and a quilted gilet.
